title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Lookup Table Demappers for Amplitude Phase-Shift Keying over Nonlinear Satellite Links
abstract: arXiv:2611.20068v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Next-generation high-throughput satellites increasingly demodulate and decode on board, so the per-symbol cost of the receiver constrains payload power and throughput. Soft demappers for nonlinear satellite links must therefore produce accurate bit log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) at low cost. We introduce a KAN-LUT demapper, a two-layer Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN) whose learned univariate edge functions are stored as 128-entry lookup tables (LUTs), so that inference needs only table reads, linear interpolation, and additions. We bound the LLR error introduced by the tables and evaluate the demapper on amplitude phase-shift keying (APSK) links with low-density parity-check (LDPC) coding and a nonlinear traveling-wave-tube amplifier. For 16-, 32-, and 64-APSK, KAN-LUT stays within 0.2 dB of a per-cluster Gaussian log-MAP (LogMAP-CG) demapper, while its cost relative to LogMAP-CG falls from 87% to 27% as the order grows. translated_title: 面向非线性卫星链路幅度相移键控的Kolmogorov-Arnold查找表解映射器
translated_abstract: 下一代高通量卫星越来越多地在星上完成解调和译码，因此接收机每符号的处理成本限制了载荷功耗与吞吐量。面向非线性卫星链路的软解映射器必须以低成本产生准确的比特对数似然比（LLR）。我们提出了一种KAN-LUT解映射器，即一个两层的Kolmogorov-Arnold网络（KAN），其学习到的单变量边缘函数被存储为128项的查找表（LUT），使得推理过程只需要查表、线性插值和加法运算。我们对查找表引入的LLR误差进行了理论界定，并在采用低密度奇偶校验（LDPC）编码和非线性行波管放大器的幅度相移键控（APSK）链路上对该解映射器进行了评估。对于16、32和64-APSK，KAN-LUT与基于簇的高斯log-MAP（LogMAP-CG）解映射器相比性能差距保持在0.2 dB以内，而其相对于LogMAP-CG的成本随调制阶数增加从87%降至27%。它匹配或……（原文摘要截断于此）
tldr: 该论文提出了一种将两层Kolmogorov-Arnold网络的边缘函数存为128项查找表的KAN-LUT软解映射器，仅需查表、线性插值和加法即可在非线性卫星APSK链路上低成本生成准确的比特LLR，性能与LogMAP-CG相差不到0.2 dB，且计算成本随调制阶数升高从87%降至27%。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a KAN-LUT soft demapper that stores the learned univariate edge functions of a two-layer Kolmogorov-Arnold network as 128-entry lookup tables, enabling accurate bit LLR computation for APSK over nonlinear satellite links at low cost—within 0.2 dB of LogMAP-CG performance while reducing computational cost from 87% to 27% as modulation order increases.
